documents.title: DePaul's Approach to Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Academic Affairs' August 2023 statement treats AI as analogous to a person under the existing integrity and research misconduct policies, says AI-generated content must be cited, and leaves allowing AI to faculty. Syllabi should state the rule, and where they are silent the general integrity policies apply.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no universal allow or ban. It says "Faculty have the discretion to allow or encourage students to use AI" and that "Course syllabi should make clear how students may or may not use AI", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: States the university's dual aim: preparing students for "a world of work in which AI will certainly play a part". This is a professional-skill rationale (P44) rather than a rule, so it is informs/neutral.
units.anchor: prepare our students for a world of work in which AI will certainly play
units.frag_start: Universities have a special challenge

units.why: The other half of the challenge: students must "understand and practice integrity in the use of any sources, including those generated by Artificial Intelligence". It sets a principle of integrity with AI sources; P56 (institution-wide framework) fits better than P36 because no misconduct classification is made here.
